title: Adaptive surge peering + proportional overage crediting for Dedicated fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Customers on Dedicated want predictable throughput but occasional spikes still occur. Current transient surge lanes are useful but cause: (1) unfair invoice spikes when multiple tenants share ephemeral capacity, (2) poor operator visibility into why specific tenants consumed surge capacity, and (3) brittle autoscaler interactions when headroom is borrowed between pools. This ticket proposes an 'adaptive surge peering' abstraction plus a proportional overage crediting model to address fairness, observability, and predictable billing.

Scope: Implement a controller that allows adjacent Dedicated pools (same region and hardware class) to peer into a shared ephemeral surge plane under a configurable policy. The controller will: (a) decide when to allow cross-tenant spill based on SLOs, current utilization, and predictive short-term forecasts, (b) tag surge allocations with provenance metadata for billing and audit, and (c) issue proportional overage credits to tenants that borrowed from the shared plane based on time-weighted usage share and pre-agreed grace policies. Integrations: autoscaler (to respect soft/hard caps), billing pipeline (to record surge usage / credit tokens), console (operator view + tenant-level invoice preview), and auditors (immutable event stream).
acceptance_criteria: Controller can form a surge peer between two or more Dedicated pools with a single config flag
When surge peering is active, requests overflow to the peer plane while origin pool maintains latency SLO >= configured threshold
All surge allocations include immutable metadata: origin_pool, peer_pool, allocation_ts, allocation_duration, token_id
Billing pipeline emits per-tenant surge usage lines and a computed proportional credit amount (time-decayed) for invoice preview
Operator console shows a timeline of surge events with filter by tenant, pool, and token_id
End-to-end integration tested with autoscaler: soft cap respected, hard cap prevents further spill and triggers graceful degradation fallback
comments: 2026-02-10 Aisha: Draft created after runbook review and two customer calls where unexpected surge invoices caused churn risk.
2026-02-12 Miguel: PoC for surge tagging completed (in dev cluster). We added 'token_id' to allocations. Early telemetry shows ~12% of surged tokens have mixed-origin that require attribution logic.
2026-02-13 Design review (Katherine): Console timeline mockups look good but we need a compact invoice preview widget — raised UI constraint to 200px height for compact screens.
2026-02-15 Infra (Ravi): Wire protocol for peer discovery uses existing placement service; adding TTL on peer leases to avoid stale peers after failures.
2026-02-16 Billing (Sofia): Proposed proportional credit algorithm using time-weighted share with exponential decay (alpha=0.3). Need finance approval for rounding rules and statement language.

2026-02-17 QA: Created stress test (50k concurrent requests) to validate latency SLO behavior when surge plane is saturated. Logging spike observed for allocation metadata serialization; Miguel to optimize path.
2026-02-18 PM (Oliver): Marking ticket In Review. Please attach PRs and test results; planning follow-up EPIC for operator tooling improvements if this lands.
billing_model_changes: Add 'surge_token' row type to billing exports with fields: token_id, origin_tenant, consumer_tenant, start_ts, end_ts, consumed_tokens. New billing pipeline job 'surge-credit-aggregator' computes credits per invoice window and emits a 'credit_note' line that gets applied before invoice finalization.
operator_playbook: To enable peering: rwctl surge peer create --origin-pool=ded-usw2-gtx --peer-pool=ded-usw2-rtx --policy=balanced --ttl=180s
Inspect active tokens: rwctl surge tokens list --pool=ded-usw2-gtx --since=1h
Force revoke peer lease: rwctl surge peer revoke --peer-lease-id=PLE-...
Generate invoice preview for tenant: rwctl billing preview --tenant=acme-corp --window=2026-02-01,2026-02-28
implementation_notes: Trade-offs considered: (1) full isolation (no peering) is simplest but wastes idle capacity; (2) naive first-come-claim causes large invoices and customer disputes; (3) proportional crediting avoids churn but requires stronger telemetry and immutable allocation events. We chose token-based allocations so billing and audit systems can replay decisions deterministically. The exponential decay in credits reduces long-tail refunds while rewarding immediate short-term borrowing.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Incorrect attribution could credit the wrong tenant -> Mitigation: Immutable token events + two-phase commit in allocation path
Risk: Surge peering amplifies noisy neighbors -> Mitigation: Policy options (balanced / priority / capped-share) and autoscaler soft caps
Risk: Finance rejects credit model -> Mitigation: Provide sample invoices for top 10 tenants and run A/B with manual approvals for two billing cycles before automatic application
